report:
### Conclusion
Current clinical evidence does not reliably demonstrate that *Ginkgo biloba* extract relieves tinnitus symptoms. 

### Scientific Evidence Overview
*Ginkgo biloba* is a widely used herbal supplement, but rigorous systematic reviews show little to no proven efficacy over a placebo:

* **Lack of Reliable Benefit:** Cochrane systematic reviews assessing randomized controlled trials found no reliable evidence that *Ginkgo biloba* reduces tinnitus severity compared to placebo. Evidence updates highlight high uncertainty regarding any potential benefits or harms for tinnitus sufferers [https://earlabs.app/articles/ginkgo-biloba-tinnitus-evidence/], [https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD013514_ginkgo-biloba-herbal-supplement-tinnitus].
* **Clinical Guidelines:** International clinical guidelines for tinnitus management generally do not endorse or include *Ginkgo biloba* due to the absence of large, independent, high-quality clinical trials showing effectiveness [https://www.evigrade.com/en/drugs/ginkgo-biloba].

In summary, while individual small studies present mixed findings, high-quality scientific consensus indicates that *Ginkgo biloba* extract is not an established or effective treatment for tinnitus symptoms.

### Sources
* The Ear Lab: https://earlabs.app/articles/ginkgo-biloba-tinnitus-evidence/
* Cochrane Review: https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD013514_ginkgo-biloba-herbal-supplement-tinnitus
* Evidence Grade Guidelines: https://www.evigrade.com/en/drugs/ginkgo-biloba
